records.label: Four-generation family

phenotypes.text: free articular bodies with joint locking
multiple epiphyseal dysplasia with hips not markedly affected at early age

variants.as_reported: G --> C substitution at position -1 in the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splicing region

records.segregation: Substitution confirmed in 8 clinically affected family members and 3 presymptomatic young children
quotes: We report on a family of 19 individuals over four generations in which 12 members are affected with a variant of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia. Beginning in childhood, the disease leads to pain and stiffness of knees, ankles, elbows and finger joints.
Some adult patients repeatedly suffer from free articular bodies resulting in locking of the joint. Finally, affected individuals are prone to the development of early degenerative joint disease.

Mutation screening of candidate regions revealed a novel point mutation at position -1 in the COL9A2 exon 3/intron 3 splicing region. This G --> C substitution most probably induces an alteration of the splicing process.
We confirmed the nucleotide substitution in eight clinically affected family members as well as in three presymptomatic young children.

notes.statement: Nakashima et al. (2005) reported that double-layered patella in multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is not exclusive to DTDST mutation.
quotes: Double-layered patella in multiple epiphyseal dysplasia is not exclusive to DTDST mutation.

notes.statement: Fiedler et al. (2002) found by electron microscopy that the diameter of collagen fibrils from arthroscopically removed free articular bodies of 2 patients was not obviously different from that of normal articular cartilage.
quotes: Electron microscopy showed that the diameter of collagen fibrils from arthroscopically removed free articular bodies of two patients was not obviously different from that of normal articular cartilage.

notes.statement: Fiedler et al. (2002) concluded that, together with previous reports, mutations leading to skipping of exon 3 within the COL3 domain of the alpha-2 chain of collagen type IX may be relatively common in patients with a subtype of MED in which the hips are not markedly affected at an early age (EDM2).
quotes: Together with previous reports our results indicate that mutations leading to skipping of exon 3 within the COL3 domain of the alpha2-chain of collagen type IX may be relatively common in patients with a special subtype of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) in which the hips are not markedly affected at early age (EDM2).

notes.statement: Fiedler et al. (2002) screened the family by automated sequencing and BsaWI digestion of amplicons, and suggested that mutation screening of candidate regions may help confirm the diagnosis of EDM2 and support lifestyle advice and genetic counseling.
quotes: Family screening was carried out by both automated sequencing and by digestion of amplicons with BsaWI.
In these patients and their families, mutation screening of the candidate regions may help to confirm the diagnosis, lead to appropriate advice for lifestyle and well based genetic counseling.

notes.statement: Muragaki et al. (1996) reported that a mutation in COL9A2, the gene encoding the alpha-2 chain of the fibril-associated collagen IX, causes multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (EDM2).
quotes: A mutation in the gene encoding the alpha 2 chain of the fibril-associated collagen IX, COL9A2, causes multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (EDM2).

notes.statement: In a large family with multiple epiphyseal dysplasia, Briggs et al. (1994) excluded linkage to the chromosome 19 interval linked to pseudoachondroplasia and a form of MED, and identified an MED locus (EDM2) on the short arm of chromosome 1, in a region containing COL9A2, which encodes the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen.
quotes: Linkage studies with the chromosome 19 markers were carried out in a large family with MED and excluded the previously identified interval.
Using this family, we have identified an MED locus on the short arm of chromosome 1, in a region containing the gene (COL9A2) that encodes the alpha 2 chain of type IX collagen

notes.statement: Briggs et al. (1994) showed that MED is genetically heterogeneous: in one large family it did not map to the chromosome 19 interval to which another form of MED and pseudoachondroplasia had been linked, but mapped to chromosome 1p.
quotes: Recently, both mild and severe PSACH as well as a form of MED have been linked to the same interval on chromosome 19, suggesting that they may be allelic disorders.

notes.statement: Briggs et al. (1994) described multiple epiphyseal dysplasia as a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia with mild short stature and early-onset osteoarthrosis. Some forms clinically resemble mild pseudoachondroplasia.
quotes: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia (MED) is a dominantly inherited chondrodysplasia characterized by mild short stature and early-onset osteoarthrosis. Some forms of MED clinically resemble another chondrodysplasia phenotype, the mild form of pseudoachondroplasia (PSACH).

notes.statement: Warman et al. (1994) used fluorescence in situ hybridization to map the COL9A2 gene, which encodes the alpha-2 chain of type IX collagen, to human chromosome 1p32.3-p33. They used a single-strand conformational polymorphism within the murine Col9a2 gene to map that gene to mouse chromosome 4.
quotes: COL9A2 was mapped to human chromosome 1p32.3-p33 using fluorescence in situ hybridization.
A single-strand conformational polymorphism within the murine Col9a2 gene was used to map this locus to mouse chromosome 4.

notes.statement: Versteylen et al. (1988) described 2 families with apparent multiple epiphyseal dysplasia in which there was a striking incidence of severe osteochondritis dissecans of the knees. They suggested that this was caused by the fragmented and maldeveloped epiphyses characteristic of epiphyseal dysplasia.
quotes: In both families a striking incidence of severe osteochondritis of the knees was encountered.
It is suggested that this was caused by the fragmented and maldeveloped epiphyses characteristic of epiphyseal dysplasia.
